target.title: policy: cover gateway node commands
target.body:
## Summary
- add policy evidence for `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` and `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` entries
- add `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` policy metadata and shape validation
- report `policy/gateway-node-command-denied` when policy-denied node commands are not denied by OpenClaw config
- classify `gateway.nodes.allowCommands.*` in policy config coverage

## Validation
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts --reporter=dot`
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-policy-config-coverage.ts --check --json`
- `./node_modules/oxfmt/bin/oxfmt --check extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/gateway.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/policy-state.ts scripts/lib/policy-config-coverage.jsonc`
- `./node_modules/oxlint/bin/oxlint extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/gateway.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/policy-state.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions`
- `codex review --base upstream/main`

## Notes
This gives managed policy a way to require privileged gateway node commands such as `system.run` to be present in `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` unless a deployment intentionally relaxes policy. The rule uses the existing `denylist-superset` strictness pattern and keeps node command IDs case-sensitive.
